_doc: Schema for claude/cycles/<cycle_id>/execution_state.json. Created by the Sprint Execution Engine at STEP 0.
_spec_references_note: spec_references may be empty (set to []) ONLY for delegated_qa documentation artefacts (test scenario files, readiness assessments) OR autonomous infrastructure/tooling items with no prior canonical spec — e.g. Case E in execution_prompt.md STEP 3.1.A (bug/correctness fixes with no governing spec and no new artefact). When leaving spec_references empty, set spec_reference_not_applicable: true and spec_reference_not_applicable_reason to a one-line rationale (added v1.1, BLG-GOV per lessons_learnt_closure.md v6.8 Phase 4 friction item — this is the structured exemption signal). The completion condition check and delivery verification must NOT flag spec_references:[] as a traceability gap when spec_reference_not_applicable is true. Legacy compatibility: for records written before this field existed, delivery verification also honours notes containing exactly 'no prior spec applicable' as an equivalent (but no longer written going forward).
_sign_off_record_note: method is 'agent_mediated' when §5.3 sign-off protocol ran, or 'human' when resolved by the user directly.
_deviations_filed_note: true means 'the deviation check was performed for this story' -- NOT literally 'a deviation record exists'. Set true on every done story regardless of whether the check found anything to file (execution_prompt.md STEP 3.1.A step 10/10a). A qa_evidence_EPIC-xx.md consolidation block reading 'Known deviations filed: None' while every story row shows deviations_filed: true is expected and consistent, not a contradiction -- to find an actual filed deviation for a specific story, read that story's qa_evidence_EPIC-xx.md row / the canonical spec's Known Deviations section, never infer presence/absence from this boolean alone. Full explanation: shared_standards.md §16.15 (canonical; kept in sync with this note).
